newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to launch Mir cargo rocket on Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Russia to launch Mir cargo rocket on Sunday.

text.p: Russia will launch a Progress-34 cargo craft on Sunday to deliver food, water, fuel and equipment to the Mir space station, a spokesman for the Military Space Forces said on Friday.
"The seven-tonne Soyuz booster is on the launching pad at the Baikonur cosmodrome and engineers have begun final pre-launch tests," he told Reuters.
The launch is scheduled for 1604 GMT on Sunday.

An official from the Russian Space Agency, which coordinates manned space flights, said obtaining fuel for the Soyuz booster which will carry the Progress into space had become a major problem at Baikonur, which Russia leases from the former Soviet republic of Kazakhstan.
"We've sent 200 tonnes of kerosene needed for the Soyuz launch from Russia because we could not get fuel in Kazakhstan," the officials said.
Currently, two Russian cosmonauts and a U.S. astronaut are working on the ageing Mir orbital station. The Progress is scheduled to dock with the Mir on April 8.
